call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer:
The project must develop a new digital ocean solution and integrate it into EDITO, the public platform at the core of the European Digital Twin Ocean, within 12 months.
EDITO is a free, public platform that gives the marine science and data community tools to build digital twins (virtual, data-driven replicas) of the ocean and to make science-based decisions. The issuing project, EDITO 2, is a Horizon Europe project (2025–2028) that passes part of its grant to third parties through this cascade call (a call in which an EU-funded project funds other organisations).
What the project must deliver:
- A digital ocean application, reusable model, workflow, API (an interface that lets other software use the data or model), dashboard, decision-support tool or dataset that addresses a key ocean or coastal challenge.
- Integration of that solution into the EDITO platform, so it is deployed, tested and usable there.
The solution must be innovative in the call's sense: it must bring clear added value to EDITO and its users. The call particularly encourages what-if scenario applications, reusable models and workflows building on Copernicus Marine, EMODnet, Destination Earth or Horizon Europe results, unique or hard-to-access datasets that are legally shareable, and decision-support applications that turn ocean data into indicators, maps, risk layers, alerts or scenarios.
The need behind the call is a policy and societal one: the EU Mission Restore our Ocean and Waters, the EU Ocean Pact and the EU Green Deal. Proposals must fall under one of seven themes:
- High seas and deep-ocean sustainability
- Coastal, island and outermost regions resilience
- Ocean extremes and early-warning services
- Marine pollution and pressure assessment
- Climate impacts and biogeochemical indicators
- Marine biodiversity, habitats and restoration
- Sustainable blue economy and maritime services
None of the themes names offshore energy or electricity grids.

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
The project must strengthen the European Digital Twin Ocean and the EU's ocean policies; the call sets no numeric targets.
The pages read state that EDITO serves the objectives of the EU Mission Restore our Ocean and Waters: protecting biodiversity, stopping marine pollution and supporting a sustainable blue economy. The seven themes are designed to support that Mission, the EU Ocean Pact and the EU Green Deal.
Funded solutions are expected to be policy-relevant and user-oriented: the call asks for developments that can be deployed, tested and integrated into EDITO, and that turn ocean data and models into decision-ready outputs for end users. Through the platform, the work is meant to help consolidate an operational, interoperable and scalable European Digital Twin Ocean. The call says nothing about energy-system outcomes such as transmission capacity or renewable integration.

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer:
It suits organisations that build ocean data products, models or applications, such as marine research institutes, universities, ocean-data companies and public bodies running ocean services.
The pages read say only that EDITO will give financial support to selected European, national, regional or local projects and initiatives that integrate innovative digital ocean solutions into the EDITO ecosystem. The pages read do not state which types of organisation may lead, whether a consortium is required, or how work and funding must be shared; these rules are in the call dossier on the Mercator Ocean submission platform, which was not opened.
The general Mercator Ocean grant rules apply: a grant must not generate profit and must be limited to what balances the project budget, it cannot fund work already completed, and each beneficiary may receive only one grant per project, with no double funding of the same costs.

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer:
The solution must be deployed, tested and integrated in the EDITO platform itself within the 12-month project.
The work is digital: the call asks for applications, models, workflows, APIs, dashboards or datasets that run in, or are served through, EDITO. Datasets must be legally shareable, well documented, interoperable and reusable within EDITO. The call encourages building on recognised European data and model infrastructures such as Copernicus Marine, EMODnet, EDITO itself and Destination Earth. The evaluation also scores usability, stakeholder engagement and the added value of integrating the proposal into EDITO, so the solution must work for real platform users rather than stand alone.

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer:
TenneT could benefit indirectly from better open marine environmental data and models for the North Sea, which offshore grid planning and permitting rely on.
TenneT's offshore grid work, such as the 2GW Program and connections like Hollandse Kust West Beta, depends on knowledge of seabed habitats, marine biodiversity and ocean conditions for routing, permitting and nature-inclusive design. Solutions funded under the themes Marine biodiversity, habitats and restoration, Ocean extremes and early-warning services, or Sustainable blue economy and maritime services could make such data easier to access through EDITO (interpretation; no theme names offshore energy). TenneT could pass the call to ocean-data partners or research institutes it works with.
TenneT cannot be shown to have a route itself: the pages read do not state who may apply, the call is aimed at ocean data and model developers, and the call text with the eligibility rules was not read because it is only on the submission platform.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The call has EUR 700,000 in total, with an indicative EUR 100,000 per thematic lot.
- Total project size: the call sets no minimum or maximum per project on the pages read.
- Grant request: proportionate to the proposed work; several proposals may be selected in the same lot (theme), and ambitious proposals are encouraged with duly justified funding.
- Funding form: a grant (financial support to third parties) paid by Mercator Ocean International on behalf of EDITO 2; the payment model is not stated on the pages read.

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The pages read set only the general Mercator Ocean grant rules.
- Caps or mandatory allocations: a grant must be limited to the amount needed to balance the project budget and may not generate profit.
- Excluded costs: work already completed before the grant, and any cost already funded by another source (no double funding); each beneficiary may receive only one grant per project.

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One mandatory stage: a single-stage application on the Mercator Ocean grants platform (achatpublic.com).
- Stage 1 — Application: 29 January 2027, 12:00 Paris time according to the Mercator Ocean platform; the Funding & Tenders Portal gives 17:00 Brussels time, so the earlier time is the safe one. Applicants submit a complete application and a technical proposal. The platform is in French only; the call documents are under "Pièces de marché" (call documents) and questions go through "Questions/Réponses" (questions and answers).

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The call does not give decision dates on the pages read; all applicants are told the outcome.
- Funding decision: an evaluation panel ranks eligible proposals and informs all applicants of the decision; unsuccessful applicants receive feedback. Results are published on the project website.

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
An assessment panel scores eligible proposals and draws up a ranking list.
- Evaluation criteria: excellence, impact, implementation, usability, stakeholder engagement, and the added value of integrating the proposal into EDITO.
- Ranking rules: proposals are ranked per the panel's scores; several proposals may be selected within the same theme, within the indicative EUR 100,000 per theme.
